## 2

I understand why the photos might look suspicious if you already distrust the agencies releasing them. But you don't need NASA to check the shape of the Earth. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon. During a lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow on the Moon is always round, which only a sphere produces from every angle. People in different time zones see the sun at different heights at the same moment, and in 240 BC Eratosthenes used that effect to estimate the Earth's circumference fairly accurately. Thousands of pilots, sailors, and amateur astronomers from rival countries would all have to be in on a fake. What evidence would change your mind? If nothing could, it's worth asking whether that's a belief about the evidence or about who you trust.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's really a mix of all the colours, and each colour is a wave with a different length. Red has long waves and blue has short ones. When sunlight comes into the atmosphere, it runs into nitrogen and oxygen molecules, which are much smaller than the light's waves. Molecules that small scatter short waves far more than long ones. Blue light gets scattered about five times more than red, so it bounces around the sky in every direction. Wherever you look, some of that scattered blue light is heading toward your eyes, and the whole sky looks blue.

Violet waves are even shorter, so why isn't the sky violet? The sun gives off less violet than blue, some violet gets absorbed high in the atmosphere, and your eyes are less sensitive to it. At sunset, the light passes through much more air to reach you, so most of the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, and the reds and oranges are what's left.

夜里十点多，雨还没有停。雨点打在窗玻璃上，声音时密时疏，像有人在外面轻轻敲门，又不肯进来。楼下的路灯被雨雾裹住，只剩一团昏黄的光，照着积水里晃动的倒影。偶尔有车开过，轮胎碾过水面，发出长长的一声，随后街道又安静下来。空气里有泥土和树叶的味道，凉凉的，从窗缝里钻进来。我关了大灯，只留一盏台灯，泡了杯热茶，坐在窗边看雨。手机放在一旁，没有消息，也不想有消息。这样的夜晚好像被雨隔开了，外面的事都远了，只剩下雨声和一杯慢慢变凉的茶。
